semantics.note: The sentence follows 'If generative AI becomes an albatross...', so the investor-questioning forecast depends on that antecedent, which the drafter dropped. The revenue part is hedged ('likely'). The $100bn is a premise he labels estimated, not a prediction.

contract.note: The contract scores the compound claim, including the hedged 'likely won't drive any revenue growth', and ignores the conditional antecedent. Policy does not score hedged language, so this is not fair to his actual words.

evidence.note: Real dated transcript, but the analyst's question about margin tradeoffs is constructive. It does not ask why the spending is happening or raise payouts as an alternative.
Reuters, Feb 2025: investors balked at Alphabet's capex plans. This supports only the investor-scrutiny component.
Microsoft's own disclosure: AI services added 16 points to Azure growth. This cuts against the hedged revenue expectation, but the category is broader than generative AI.

reviews.rationale: The revenue expectation is hedged ('likely'), so it is not scored. The investor-questioning forecast depends on 'If generative AI becomes an albatross', and the packet does not show that condition happened. Under policy neither part can be scored, even though e2 shows investors were questioning the spending.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'starting to see', the 'point of failure' wording, the named firms and Apple's lesser role. It is a present-tense observation about an emerging trend.

contract.note: Reading the metaphor as growing dependence on a few big tech firms for compute, financing and distribution is ordinary and fair. The 2024 reporting window is the evaluator's choice.

evidence.note: UK CMA paper, April 2024, inside the target period. It documents growing vertical integration and 90+ partnerships tying model developers to the GAMMAN firms. It is a regulatory report rather than statistics, and it also notes possible pro-competitive benefits.

reviews.rationale: The CMA's April 2024 findings show developers increasingly tied to Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Apple through partnerships, investments and cloud dependence. That matches the plain reading of a starting shift toward a few firms. No counterevidence shows the trend running the other way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'Will have to come through' is firm language. The proposition keeps the $5bn-to-$10bn need, the end-2025 horizon and the three named channels.

contract.note: Counting VC-held convertible notes as 'private debt' stretches the words in his favour. In context he set those channels against venture and Microsoft money. Requiring reconciled minimum-survival cash records also asks for something no available evidence can show.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure of the $6.6B raised. It shows funding obtained, not the minimum OpenAI needed to survive.
Reuters: the Oct 2024 round came largely from Thrive, Khosla, Microsoft, Nvidia, Altimeter and Fidelity, beyond the named channels, although SoftBank also took part.
A $4B bank credit facility, undrawn at closing. It shows debt was available, but no cash was received.
SoftBank's own disclosure: it fully funded its 2025 commitment before the deadline. This supports SoftBank as a major channel.

reviews.rationale: Holds: SoftBank became a major funder in 2025 (e4). Fails on the ordinary reading: a round above $5B came mostly from VCs, Microsoft and Nvidia, outside the channels he said money would 'have to' come through (e2). Not established: the $5bn-to-$10bn survival need.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'possible' GPT-5 hedge and the 'potential customers' scope. 'Desperately needs' is evaluative framing; the checkable core is what customers believed at the time.

contract.note: Telling 'no significant jump' apart from 'a smaller jump than GPT-3 to GPT-4' is an ordinary and fair reading of his words.

evidence.note: Derivative secondary summary dated July 2024. Heller: better, though not necessarily game-changing. Consistent with e2, but weak provenance.

Business Insider Spain's edition of the customer-interview report. Heller expects GPT-5 to be clearly better (the undergrad-to-PhD comparison, more agentic ability), and his doubt is only whether it will feel as big as the last leap.

reviews.rationale: The customer in the interview reporting expected a clear, practical improvement over GPT-4; his reservation was whether the leap would match GPT-3 to GPT-4. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. The 'desperately needs' framing cannot be tested.
